root_cause_label: Numerical noise injection in optimize() violates exact-probability test assertions; subplan caching abandoned
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented optimize() with a self.probs += 1e-6 noise term that prevents probabilities from reaching exactly 0 or 1, causing persistent failures in tests that assert deterministic elite convergence, while also abandoning the required subplan caching in evaluate_plans_memoized.
t_err_evidence: Step 16 introduces the optimize() method with two bugs: (1) wrong number of sampled plans (samples horizon plans not num_samples), and (2) adds self.probs += 1e-6 noise followed by renormalization, causing probabilities to never be exactly 0 or 1 — the noise persists in all subsequent rewrites (steps 17, 19, 21).
t_commit_evidence: The noise addition pattern (self.probs += 1e-6; self.probs /= sum) is introduced in step 16 and carried forward verbatim in steps 17, 19, and 21 through the end of the trajectory; no step removes it, locking in the failure.
t_surface_evidence: Step 18 runs all tests and shows test_q2_cross_entropy_optimize.py FFFFFFF (7/7 failing), with the specific error: optimizer.probs showing ~1e-5 minimum values instead of exact 0 due to the noise term.
trigger_explanation: The agent correctly understands the CEM algorithm conceptually but generates code with a subtle but fatal implementation flaw: adding small numerical noise to prevent zero-probabilities (a heuristic sometimes used in practice) breaks the test suite's exact assertions. This reflects a code generation quality failure — the agent applies a non-standard practice that violates the spec's implicit requirement that probabilities can reach exact 0/1 values.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 5-6: first sed command produces malformed code (step indented inside reset body); step 6 shows AttributeError. Steps 8-10: agent overwrites cross_entropy.py with test file content by mistake, leading to ImportError. Steps 9-10: second sed attempt still fails. These repeated command failures signal unreliable editing approach before the critical implementation at step 16.
